The Assessor reports that countywide assessed value rose about 1.2 percent for 2026, and that most of the increase in tax bills comes from voter-approved measures rather than value growth. Every year staff physically inspect one-sixth of the county; area 5, which included mid-Bellingham, Geneva and Sudden Valley, was inspected in 2026 and area 6 comes in 2027.

How do I appeal a Whatcom County assessment?

File a petition with the county Board of Equalization on the state form. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days after the value notice was mailed, or within a longer period of up to 60 days if the county legislative authority adopted one, whichever is later. For the 2025 assessment year the county posted an October 27, 2025 deadline, which has passed. Your Change of Value notice states the deadline that applies to you, so read it as soon as it arrives.

The Board must value property at 100 percent of market value and may lower, raise or keep the value. A late petition can be accepted for good cause such as serious illness, a natural disaster or postal delay. Appeals of the Board's decision go to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals. Before filing, talk to an appraiser at the Assessor's office, because the Assessor values property at 100 percent of market value and can explain how your number was reached.

What tax relief is available to Whatcom County homeowners?

Two programs matter most for people selling under financial strain.

  • Senior and disability exemption. For 2026 taxes the prior qualifications still apply. A 2026 law change raises the income limit to $72,000 starting with 2026 income, which affects 2027 taxes, adds a standard deduction of $7,500 per person or $15,000 per couple, lowers the veteran disability rating that qualifies from 80 to 40 percent, and exempts participants from the state school levy in full. Three income levels, $54,000, $63,000 and $72,000, set how much assessed value is exempt from regular levies. Apply through the Assessor in person or online.
  • Destroyed property. After the December 2025 flooding, the Assessor lowered values on affected parcels in Sumas, Nooksack, Everson and Ferndale for the 2025/26 year. Values return to market for 2027 taxes. The Assessor's destroyed property coordinator handles claims for parcels that are still damaged.

Washington also runs a property tax deferral program under chapter 84.38 RCW, which each tax statement must mention. Ask the Assessor's office whether you qualify.

How are taxes handled when I sell a Whatcom County house?

Any transfer of property needs a real estate excise tax affidavit filed with the Treasurer, with payment, before the deed is recorded at the County Auditor. The Treasurer will not accept an incomplete affidavit or give legal advice on filling it out. You have 30 days from the date of sale before interest and penalty begin. Ask your escrow or title officer to request a payoff from the Treasurer for any delinquent years and the current half before the closing date.

Gift transfers also require a supplemental statement signed by both parties, and a minimum filing fee applies if no tax is due. Mobile homes have their own steps: one that will be moved needs a tax certificate from the Assessor and an orange decal from the Treasurer. For state rates and exemptions, see the Washington real estate excise tax page and the county's excise tax page.

More questions about Whatcom County, WA Property Tax Guide

When are property taxes due in Whatcom County?

April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day. Mailed payments count on the post office postmark date.

What happens if I do not pay Whatcom County property tax?

Interest starts after the due date, 9 percent per year on a home with four or fewer units. Foreclosure begins once taxes are three years delinquent, and the Treasurer holds the auction each November. Income-qualified owners living in the home can ask about a waiver of interest and penalties.

How do I check what I owe in Whatcom County?

Use the Treasurer's online tax lookup or call 360-778-5160. Property tax records are public records. Ask for the payoff for each delinquent year as well as the current year if you are selling.

Can I appeal my Whatcom County property value?

Yes, through the Board of Equalization. The deadline is stated on your Change of Value notice and is the later of July 1 or 30 days after the notice, or up to 60 days if the county set that period. The Assessor's office at 360-778-5050 can review the value with you first.

Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Whatcom County house sells?

The seller pays. The Treasurer collects it with an affidavit before the deed is recorded, and interest and penalty start after 30 days from the date of sale. Your escrow company normally takes it out of the seller's proceeds.

Spokane County by the numbers

Where is Spokane County and who lives there?

Spokane County is in eastern Washington, with the city of Spokane as both county seat and largest city. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 558,344 residents, which makes it the fourth-most populous county in the state, and it covers about 1,764 square miles of land. Mount Spokane, at 5,883 feet, is the highest point.

The county was created by the territorial legislature in 1858 from part of Walla Walla County, was attached to Stevens County for a time, and became separate again on October 30, 1879. Outside the city, residential communities include Nine Mile Falls, Newman Lake, Greenacres, Peone and Veradale. Schools are divided among many districts, among them Spokane Public Schools, Central Valley, Mead, East Valley, West Valley, Cheney, Deer Park and Medical Lake, and the district you live in affects the school levy on your bill.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owner-occupied home value of $410,700, a median household income of $78,582 and an owner-occupied rate of 64.5%. The county had 241,434 housing units in 2025, and the Assessor says it appraises about 212,000 real property parcels.

Which Spokane County offices handle property tax?

The Assessor values property, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Board of Equalization is an independent body that handles appeals. About 56 taxing districts in the county send budgets to the Assessor each November, and the Assessor turns them into levy rates in January.

  • Treasurer: Spokane County Courthouse, 1116 W. Broadway Ave., Spokane, WA 99260; 509-477-4713; treasurer@spokanecounty.gov; open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698 for ownership, values and exemptions; 509-477-4787 for business personal property.
  • Mail payments go to the Spokane County Treasurer, P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210.

The Treasurer's office will be closed Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, 2026, for Thanksgiving, and reopens Monday, November 30, at 8:30 a.m.

When are Spokane County property taxes due?

Spokane County taxes are due in two halves, April 30 and October 31. If the total is under $50, the whole amount is due April 30. A due date that lands on a weekend or county holiday moves to the next business day. October 31, 2026 fell on a Saturday, and the second half for 2026 is now past.

The county mails one statement a year with a coupon for each half. If you have not received it by March 31, call 509-477-4713 or look it up on the SCOUT site, because a missing statement does not excuse late payment. Owners who pay through a mortgage escrow still receive a full statement, and under Washington law it is the taxpayer's responsibility to make sure the tax is paid.

Payment options include online (eCheck, debit or credit card), phone, mail, the courthouse, and two drop boxes at the courthouse that take checks only. In April and October the Treasurer also collects in person at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library on set dates. Online fees are charged by the vendor: 45 cents per eCheck transaction, and 2.65% on cards with a $1.00 minimum. Mailed payments are sorted by federal postmark under RCW 1.12.070, and a postage meter date does not count, so mail early.

What happens when a Spokane County payment is late?

First-half tax becomes delinquent on May 1 and second-half tax on November 1. Interest is figured on the full year's tax.

ChargeResidential, four or fewer units, and manufactured homesOther real property and personal property
Interest0.75% per month (9% a year) on current-year taxes1% per month (12% a year)
PenaltyNone3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1

Source: Spokane County Treasurer, Homeowner Information. Taxes billed before 2023 accrue at 1% per month.

The county says it cannot waive interest or penalty when it mailed the statement to an address supplied by the taxpayer or a taxpayer's agent, such as a closing agent. A hardship waiver exists for a personal residence if the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent caused the missed payment, but the treasurer must be told within 60 days of the due date and the tax paid within that time (RCW 84.56.025). To keep a right to sue for a refund, a payment under protest must be put in writing and included with the payment (RCW 84.68.020). A returned bank item adds a $30 fee.

How does the Spokane County Assessor value a house?

The Assessor values every real property parcel each year as of January 1, and physically inspects each at least once every six years. New construction is appraised annually, and owners are notified when a value changes. State law requires 100% of true and fair market value, based on comparable sales, depreciated replacement cost or income methods.

The Official Assessment Notice arrives in June, but levy rates are not calculated until mid-January of the following year, so the notice cannot tell you the final tax. Individual bills are not capped at a 1% increase. That limit applies to some taxing district budgets, and special levies, banked capacity and annexations complicate it.

When a market cools or stalls, assessed values follow. The Assessor's office says its values reflect sales information, and a flat local market produces flat assessments.

How do you appeal a Spokane County assessment?

You appeal to the County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the date the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. A mailed petition must be postmarked by midnight of the deadline, or you can hand-deliver it and have it date-stamped. The filing is free, and a letter or phone call does not replace the petition form.

  • Your petition must give specific reasons the value is wrong, with the parcel number, the Assessor's value and your own estimate. Tax amount, other properties' values, the size of the increase and hardship cannot be considered.
  • Extra evidence must reach the board at least seven business days before the hearing.
  • You are notified of the hearing 15 business days ahead, and a written decision usually follows within about two weeks.
  • You may settle with the Assessor by a stipulation of value, or end the appeal by withdrawal.
  • You have 30 calendar days to appeal the board's decision to the State Board of Tax Appeals, or you can pay under protest and sue for a refund under chapter 84.68 RCW.

The assessor is presumed correct, and you need clear, cogent and convincing evidence (RCW 84.40.0301). Keep paying while the case is open. One exception matters to buyers: the board can reconvene after the deadline if a new purchaser bought after July 1 and before December 31 of the assessment year at less than 90% of the assessed value.

Which relief programs help Spokane County homeowners?

The Assessor's FAQ describes a senior exemption for owner-occupants age 62 or older with household income under $50,000, available through an application on the Assessor's forms page or by calling 509-477-3698. The Treasurer's site adds that Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, sets new income thresholds for the senior and disabled persons exemption starting in 2027. Call the Assessor for the current limits, since the numbers are changing.

The exemption also reaches people retired due to disability and certain veterans. A processed application produces a corrected statement from the Treasurer for you or your mortgage company. State law additionally requires every tax statement to describe the exemption and the deferral program (RCW 84.56.020).

If you pay off a mortgage during the year, you must contact the Treasurer to update billing information and request a duplicate bill. Failure to receive a bill does not cancel interest and penalty charges.

What should you know about back taxes before selling in Spokane County?

Get a written payoff for every unpaid year from the Treasurer before closing, and have the closing agent pay it from the proceeds. Because interest accrues monthly, the figure changes each month.

The county's own rule about mailed statements has a closing-day consequence: if the Treasurer mails a bill to the address a closing agent provided and it goes unpaid, the county cannot waive the interest. Make sure your agent has the right parcel number and a forwarding address that works.

Real estate excise tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, usually from the seller. The state portion is graduated. In the schedule for sales from January 1, 2027, the 1.28% bracket applies to the price between $551,000 and $1,551,000, and the local rate comes on top. Ask the Treasurer for the total.

If taxes stay unpaid for three years from delinquency, RCW 84.64.050 requires the treasurer to issue certificates of delinquency and begin foreclosure. Payments on past-due taxes must include the oldest delinquent year, with interest and penalties, before a certificate is filed or property is distrained (RCW 84.56.020).

More questions about Spokane County, WA Property Tax Guide

When are Spokane County property taxes due?

April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. A bill under $50 is due in full April 30. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, and the next is April 30, 2027, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend.

What if I never received my Spokane County tax statement?

Call the Treasurer at 509-477-4713 or find the statement on the SCOUT site if it has not arrived by March 31. A missing bill does not cancel interest or penalty, because it remains your responsibility to see the tax is paid.

How long do I have to appeal my Spokane County assessment?

Until July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. File the Board of Equalization petition form, which is free, and keep paying your tax while the appeal runs.

What interest does Spokane County charge on late tax?

A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% a month with no penalty. Other property pays 1% a month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1. Interest is calculated on the full year's tax, starting May 1 for the first half.

Can I sell a Spokane County house that owes back taxes?

Yes, if the unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid at closing. Get a payoff from the Treasurer at 509-477-4713, and note that three years of delinquency lets the county begin foreclosure. Pay or sell before then.

Thurston County by the numbers

Which Thurston County offices handle property tax?

Three offices share the work, and all three are in the Atrium building at 3000 Pacific Ave SE in Olympia. The Treasurer bills and collects, the Assessor values property and runs exemptions, and the Board of Equalization hears value appeals.

The county announced that 2026 tax notices went out on February 9, 2026, and that the total assessed for all taxing districts was $652,290,192.

What kind of county is Thurston County?

Thurston County sits at the south end of Puget Sound along the I-5 corridor, with Olympia, the state capital, as county seat. Wikipedia's county entry lists Lacey, Tumwater, Yelm and Bucoda among the other incorporated places and notes that Lacey, with an estimated population above 60,000, has passed Olympia as the largest city. More than 145,000 people live in unincorporated areas, mostly between Olympia and Lacey.

The same entry says state government became the county's largest employment sector in the 1950s, which helps explain a housing market tied to Olympia area jobs. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table gives the current picture:

When are Thurston County property taxes due?

The Treasurer's FAQ page adds that a due date landing on a Saturday or Sunday moves to the following Monday. October 31, 2026 fell on a Saturday, so under that rule the second-half deadline became Monday, November 2, 2026, which has passed.

Sources: Thurston County Treasurer FAQ and the 2026 notice press release. Half payments are valid for the current year amount only until October 30, and real property taxes paid after that date must cover the whole year's balance. The county says the law allows no hardship extensions.

What happens when Thurston County taxes are late?

Interest runs on the whole year's tax from the date of delinquency, and real property can be sold for taxes once it is three full years behind. State law sets residential interest at 9 percent a year for properties with four or fewer units, with penalties of 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1 applying to other property types, as spelled out in RCW 84.56.020. The county FAQ describes the June and December penalties more generally, so call 360-786-5550 for the exact amount on your parcel.

  • A late payment has to include the late fees, or the Treasurer returns it.
  • Foreclosure on real property starts in June of each year and ends with a sale in the second week of January.

  • The county does not report delinquent tax to credit agencies, but the owner's name appears in a legal notice in a local newspaper.
  • If the sale brings in more than the tax and costs, the surplus goes to the owner.

The FAQ also points out that special assessments on the bill, such as stormwater, state forest fire protection, noxious weed control, conservation district, drainage district, lake management and septic program charges, are enforceable liens. The Treasurer will not accept tax alone without them.

How do you appeal a Thurston County assessment?

You file a signed petition with the Board of Equalization by July 1 or 60 days after the Assessor mails the value notice, whichever is later. For the 2026 assessment year the Assessor mailed notices on September 16, 2026, and the board's 2026 appeals page set the deadline at 5 p.m. on Monday, November 16, 2026. If you are reading this after that date, the 2026 window has closed, and the late-filing rules below apply.

  • Use the county petition form with a handwritten signature, plus a copy of the front page of the value notice.
  • No email, fax or online filing is accepted for 2026. Mail, courier or hand delivery are the routes, and a mailed petition must be postmarked by the deadline.
  • File a separate petition for each parcel.
  • The board looks at market value only. It cannot consider the amount of tax, other properties' assessments, the percentage increase or personal hardship.

The county says hearings can take 12 to 18 months to be scheduled, and the Assessor's value is presumed correct, so the owner must bring clear, cogent and convincing evidence such as comparable sales, repair bids and photos. Late filing exceptions are limited and must be requested by April 30 of the following year. A decision can be appealed to the State Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days.

What property tax relief does Thurston County offer?

The senior and disability exemption is the largest program, and the Assessor runs it. Under the county's relief programs page, you qualify if you are 61 or older, or disabled and unable to work, or a disabled veteran rated 80 percent or higher (40 percent beginning in 2027). You also have to own and live in the home and have combined disposable income of $59,000 or less, rising to $83,000 beginning in 2027.

The Treasurer's FAQ says qualifying owners are exempt from voted taxes, which average about 40 percent of a Thurston County bill, and the program freezes the taxable value of the home. You still owe whatever is billed on the due date while an application is pending, and a refund follows if the Assessor approves it later.

Other programs worth asking about:

  • Senior and limited-income deferral, where the state pays the second half and places a lien. The limited-income version has a $57,000 income cap and requires five years of ownership.
  • Destroyed property relief, claimed within three years of the damage.
  • A three-year residential remodeling exemption, which must be filed before the work is done.
  • Current use classification for farm, timber and open space land.

How does property tax work at a Thurston County closing?

The Treasurer's FAQ says taxes follow the property rather than the person, and that you and the buyer decide in the closing how the year is split. Washington's default under RCW 84.60.020 prorates by the portion of the calendar year before and after the sale date, with the lien attaching on January 1.

Thurston County sends statements only once a year, in February, to the owner on record as of December 31. After a sale the new owner may not receive a bill, so tell the escrow officer which half remains open and let the title company confirm with the Treasurer. Name changes on the tax roll come through the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit filed with the county.

October 31, 2026 fell on a Saturday, so the due date moved to Monday, November 2 under the county's weekend rule. That date has passed, so call the Treasurer at 360-786-5550 for your current balance and any late charges.

Can I get an extension on Thurston County property tax?

No. The Treasurer states that the law allows no extensions for hardship. A payment plan is available for delinquent prior years, and the senior and disability exemption or deferral may reduce or postpone tax if you qualify.

When can I appeal my Thurston County assessed value?

Each year, by July 1 or 60 days from the notice mailing date. The 2026 notices went out September 16, and the board's deadline was 5 p.m. on November 16, 2026. File every year you disagree, because each petition stands alone.

How long before Thurston County forecloses on unpaid property tax?

Real property becomes subject to sale when taxes are three full years delinquent. Foreclosure begins in June and the sale is held in the second week of January. Personal property and mobile homes can be collected as soon as they are late.

Who pays Thurston County property tax when a house sells mid-year?

Unless the contract says otherwise, the seller covers the part of the year before the sale date and the buyer covers the rest. The escrow officer settles the open half with the Treasurer, who sends statements once a year in February.

Douglas County by the numbers

Where is Douglas County, Washington, and what towns does it include?

Douglas County lies on the Columbia River in north-central Washington. Waterville is the county seat, but East Wenatchee is the largest settlement, and the county is part of the Wenatchee metropolitan statistical area.

The county was created out of Lincoln County on November 28, 1883, and named for the statesman Stephen A. Douglas. The county's Wikipedia entry lists a total area of 1,849 square miles, of which 1,819 is land. Okanogan County lies to the north, Grant to the south, Kittitas to the southwest and Chelan to the west. U.S. 2 and U.S. 97 are the main highways.

Three cities sit inside the county: Bridgeport, East Wenatchee and Rock Island. Mansfield, Waterville and part of Coulee Dam are towns. Unincorporated communities include Beebe, Douglas, Lamoine, Leahy, Orondo, Palisades and Withrow. The city or town a parcel falls in matters when you sell, because the local excise tax rate changes by location.

How many people live in Douglas County, and how many own their homes?

The 2020 census counted 42,938 residents in Douglas County, up from 38,431 in 2010, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 46,473. About 74.6% of residents lived in urban areas and 25.4% in rural ones.

The county had 17,318 housing units in 2020, of which 11.0% were vacant. Among occupied units, 70.7% were owner-occupied and 29.3% were rented. About 18.0% of residents were 65 or older.

Which Douglas County offices handle property tax?

Douglas County splits the work among the Assessor, the Treasurer, the Auditor and a Board of Equalization. Most offices sit in Waterville on South Rainier Street.

  • Assessor: 213 S Rainier Street, mailing address P.O. Box 387, Waterville. Phone 509-745-8521, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The assessor is Jim Ruud.
  • Treasurer: same building, mailing address P.O. Box 609. Phone 509-745-8525. Felisha L. Rosales is the treasurer. The office also collects excise tax for the state and runs tax foreclosures.
  • Auditor: records deeds. Phone 509-745-8527.
  • Board of Equalization: 203 S Rainier, Waterville, P.O. Box 747. Phone 509-745-8537.

The Treasurer also works under contract for five irrigation districts in the county, so some bills carry irrigation charges alongside the property tax.

How does the Douglas County Assessor value a house?

Washington requires the Assessor to value property at 100% of market value, and Douglas County revalues every property each year. The Assessor's page invites owners to call 509-745-8521 to discuss a valuation before appealing.

Tax breaks start with age and income. Residents 61 or older, people retired because of a disability, and veterans with a qualifying disability may be eligible for a senior property tax exemption depending on household income. The Assessor's page links an online screening tool, but the office makes the final call. Agricultural land may qualify for open space treatment, and the Assessor has forms for current use, parcel combinations, destroyed property and address changes.

Property tax pays for cities, the county, fire protection, law enforcement, libraries, parks, roads and schools. Which of those a parcel pays for depends on where it sits.

When are Douglas County property taxes due, and how can you pay?

The first half was due April 30, 2026, and the second half October 31, 2026. October 31 fell on a Saturday this year, so ask the Treasurer how a payment dated Monday, November 2 is handled if you have not yet paid.

The Treasurer takes payment through Point and Pay by phone at 866-898-2916 or online through the TaxSifter parcel search. Payments must be processed before 11:59 p.m. Pacific time to count as same day, but they are not posted in real time, so allow two to three business days. Vendor fees are a flat $2.30 for an eCheck, 2.7% for a credit card and 0.95% for a debit card. A live-agent Personal Teller service costs an extra $5.

Under RCW 84.56.020, a missed first half makes the whole year's tax delinquent, and interest is computed monthly. Residential property of four units or fewer pays 9% a year and no penalties, while other property pays 12% plus penalties of 3% and then 8%.

How do you appeal a Douglas County assessment?

The Kitsap County Treasurer collects property tax, and the Kitsap County Assessor sets the value the bill is built on. Both offices work from the Administration Building at 619 Division Street in Port Orchard, and both answer at (360) 337-5777.

What should a Kitsap County seller know about the county itself?

Kitsap County is a peninsula county on Puget Sound, and your tax bill reflects a place with a lot of shoreline and a lot of commuters. The county was formed on January 16, 1857, and it covers the Kitsap Peninsula plus Bainbridge Island. The shoreline runs about 250 miles, and by land area the county is the fourth smallest in the state.

The incorporated cities are Bainbridge Island, Bremerton, Poulsbo and the county seat, Port Orchard. The part north of Silverdale is called North Kitsap and the part south of Bremerton is South Kitsap. Washington State Ferries and Kitsap Transit connect the county to Seattle and Edmonds.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for Kitsap County give a sense of the market a buyer sees:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 283,374, up 2.8% from the April 2020 base.
  • Land area: 395.10 square miles, or 697.6 people per square mile in 2020.

When are Kitsap County property taxes due?

Payment counts as on time if it is postmarked by the due date. The Treasurer suggests handing a letter to the post office clerk on the last day. A bank bill-pay service may mail a paper check, so set it up well ahead. The 2026 second-half date has already passed, so any unpaid balance on a parcel you plan to sell is now delinquent.

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, the county does not send the lender a copy of your statement. The lender downloads account data from the county site, and the Treasurer tells owners to read escrow statements closely, especially after buying or refinancing.

Non-residential property and residential property with more than four units pays 1% per month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1.

The Treasurer says there is no good-cause waiver, and not receiving a statement does not erase interest. The listed exceptions are narrow:

  • The county made an error and never sent the notice.
  • One missed payment on a personal residence after the death of a spouse, or of a parent or stepparent, if the Treasurer hears about it within 60 days of the due date and receives a death certificate.
  • An underpayment caused by an apparent taxpayer error, paid within 30 days of notice.
  • Military owners stationed abroad during an armed conflict.

You can pay the current year without clearing older years, but a tax year that reaches three years late can be sent to foreclosure.

How do I appeal my Kitsap County assessed value?

File a petition with the Kitsap County Board of Equalization. The deadline is July 1 of the assessment year or 60 days after the date on your value change notice, whichever is later. Kitsap uses the 60-day option that state law allows counties to adopt under RCW 84.40.038.

For the 2026 assessment year, the Assessor mailed notices on June 26, 2026, and the Board set August 31, 2026 as the last day, so that window has closed. Notices for the next assessment year should arrive in 2027, and the new deadline will print on that notice. The Board's page lays out the process:

  • There is no filing fee, and each parcel needs its own petition with a copy of the notice attached.
  • The only question is market value on the valuation date, January 1 of the assessment year.
  • Useful evidence includes comparable sales close to that date, repair estimates, easement deeds, appraisals and photographs.
  • Hearings run Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., on the fourth floor of the Administration Building or by phone.
  • Decisions usually arrive within two weeks, and state law allows 45 days.

The Assessor is presumed correct, so the burden of proof sits with you. If you disagree with the Board's decision, an appeal to the State Board of Tax Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the mailing date. Call the Board at 360-337-4424.

Which Kitsap County relief programs matter when you are selling?

The Assessor manages six programs, and a few of them change what you owe at sale. The ones listed on the Treasurer's FAQ are the senior and disabled persons exemption and deferral, the limited-income homeowner deferral, current use for farm, open space and forest land, the residential improvement exemption, the destroyed property exemption, and nonprofit exemptions.

The senior and disabled exemption under RCW 84.36.381 is open to owners who are at least 61 years old, retired because of a disability, or a veteran receiving VA compensation at the qualifying rating. It is tied to a principal residence you own, and the claimant can carry the exemption to a replacement home after a sale. Income limits and the share of value exempted change with the 2026 legislation that applies to taxes payable in 2027, so ask the Assessor for the current figures before you count on a number.

How does the real estate excise tax work on a Kitsap County sale?

The seller owes real estate excise tax, and it must be paid before the deed can be recorded. Kitsap County's local portion is 0.50%, and the state portion is graduated. Payment is due within 30 days of the date on the conveying document, and a $5 state technology fee applies. The Treasurer collects it at the Port Orchard counter by cash or check, and card payments carry fees.

Both parties sign a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit. Since August 1, 2023, Kitsap County also requires that affidavit when it processes a Lack of Probate Affidavit, which matters for inherited homes. For sales that close on or after January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue lists these state rates by slice of the selling price:

  • Up to $551,000 of the selling price: 1.1%.
  • $551,001 to $1,551,000: 1.28%.
  • $1,551,001 to $3,051,000: 2.75%.
  • Above $3,051,000: 3.0%.

Source: Washington Department of Revenue. Agricultural and timberland keeps a flat 1.28% state rate, and the local rate is added on top. Closings earlier than 2027 use the previous thresholds, so confirm the figure with the Treasurer or your escrow officer.

What happens if Kitsap County property taxes stay unpaid?

Once a tax year is three years late, the Treasurer begins foreclosure under chapter 84.64 RCW. As the Treasurer explains it, the full 2023 year and earlier were the at-risk years as of January 2026, and paying only those years by April 30 stops the process.

The county files foreclosure in May and serves every party with a recorded interest by certified mail, and a notice is published in the local paper. Until close of business on the last business day before the sale, the owner or any recorded interest holder can redeem by paying all taxes, interest, penalties and costs in certified funds. Personal checks are refused. After the sale, prior owners lose their rights, except minors and people a court has found incompetent, who have three years to redeem.

The Treasurer's calendar lists a tax foreclosure auction for January 26, 2027 at publicsurplus.com, with January 25, 2027 as the last day to redeem. If older years are delinquent on a home you own, a sale before foreclosure is filed is still an option.

The office also acts as the Department of Revenue's agent for the real estate excise tax on property transfers, and it runs the foreclosure process on parcels that fall three years behind. Statements for each tax year should reach owners on or before March 15 under RCW 84.56.020, provided the levy certifications arrive on time.

What is Adams County like for a property owner?

Adams County is a wheat and irrigated farming county in eastern Washington, about 1,925 square miles of land with roughly 11 people per square mile. Ritzville is the county seat, in the northeast corner where Interstate 90 meets U.S. 395, and Othello in the southwest is the largest city. Hatton, Lind and Washtucna are the towns. Lincoln County lies to the north, Whitman to the east, Franklin to the south and Grant to the west.

The county was carved out of Whitman County in November 1883. By 1904 Ritzville had become the largest initial wheat shipping point in the country, and dryland farmers left fields fallow in alternate years to hold moisture. The federal Columbia Basin Project, approved in 1943, reached the county in 1946 with the East Low Canal and Potholes East Canal, and irrigated crops pushed population up by about 12,500 between 1940 and 2010. The present art-deco courthouse in Ritzville dates from 1940.

Census figures show 21,488 residents in July 2025 and 7,220 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median value of an owner-occupied home was $273,300, 69.3 percent of homes were owner-occupied and median household income was $66,136. Only 33 building permits were issued in 2025, and 93.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

The full tax is due by April 30, and a bill over $50 can be split, with half due April 30 and the rest by October 31. What happens to taxes and excise tax when you sell in Adams County?

The property tax lien runs from January 1, and unless the sale contract says otherwise, the seller owes the share of that year's tax for the days before the sale and the buyer owes the rest (RCW 84.60.020). Most contracts and escrow instructions settle this directly, so read yours.

That last rule matters in a county built on farmland. Sellers of wheat ground or irrigated parcels should call the Assessor before the closing date, not after.

How do you challenge an assessed value in Adams County?

You petition the county board of equalization on a Department of Revenue form. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due by July 1 of the assessment year, within 30 days after the notice was mailed or sent electronically, or within a county-adopted limit of up to 60 days, whichever is latest.

  • A person who sells or is displaced from a home can transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, though no one may claim it on more than one home in a year.
  • Tax statements carry a notice about the state deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.
  • For help with a mortgage or tax problem, the Washington Homeownership Resource Center answers at 877-894-4663.

What happens when Adams County taxes go unpaid for three years?

The Treasurer starts foreclosure. In July the Certificate of Delinquency is filed with Adams County Superior Court, foreclosure costs begin to accrue, and a title search is run on each parcel. Everyone with a recorded interest is served by certified mail, and the notice is also published in the county's official newspaper.

  • The court enters a judgment foreclosing the tax lien and authorizing a public auction.
  • Owners and others with a legal interest can redeem until the close of business the day before the sale.
  • Parcels that do not sell become Tax Title Property held in trust by the county, and a list is available by emailing the Treasurer.
  • A certificate of delinquency cannot be filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less, excluding interest and penalties (RCW 84.64.050).

Personal property is handled differently: the treasurer is directed to seize and sell it once those taxes turn delinquent.

The seller usually pays, and the buyer becomes responsible if the seller does not. The Treasurer collects it with the affidavit before the Auditor records the deed. The local share is 0.25 percent of the sale price, with a $5 processing fee.

Three full years. After that the Treasurer files a Certificate of Delinquency with the Superior Court in July, and the owner can redeem until the close of business the day before the auction.

If a mortgage company pays your taxes you will not get a bill, so call the office if you expect a statement and nothing has come by mid-March.

What kind of county is Lewis County for a home seller?

Lewis County is a large, mostly rural county in Southwest Washington built along the Interstate 5 corridor. Chehalis is the county seat and Centralia is the largest city. The county covers about 2,403 square miles of land and touches eight other counties, and the Cascade Mountains and the Chehalis, Cowlitz and Nisqually river systems are part of its geography.

The statement for 2026 was scheduled to go out around February 13. The county offers e-statements and ACH payment, which draws the tax from a checking or savings account on the due date. Mail payments to the Lewis County Treasurer, PO Box 509, Chehalis, WA 98532, and mail them early, since the county measures timeliness by postmark.

What happens if I pay late in Lewis County?

Interest starts the first of the next month and is charged monthly on the unpaid tax. Residential property with four or fewer units, including mobile homes, pays 0.75% per month with no penalty. Nonresidential property and residential property with more than four units pays 1% per month, a one-time 3% penalty if still unpaid on June 1, and another one-time 8% if unpaid on December 1.

The Board mails a hearing notice at least 30 days ahead. Hearings are held on Thursdays and Fridays, and evidence must arrive at least 21 business days before yours. The decision follows within 45 days, and a further appeal to the State Board of Tax Appeals is due within 30 days of the postmark.

The county's guide is blunt about what counts. The question is market value, and comparable sales from 2025 in your area carry the most weight. A neighbor's value, a percentage increase, hardship or the size of your bill do not establish market value. The Assessor's valuation is presumed correct, so you need clear, cogent and convincing evidence. Staff encourage a call to the Assessor first, because an agreement can let you withdraw the petition.

What counts as land and improvements on a Lewis County valuation notice?

The Assessor values land and improvements separately, and in Lewis County the word improvements covers more than the house. It includes garages, barns and outbuildings, wells, septic systems, utilities and driveways. Land is valued as if it were bare, so trees, vegetation and landscaping are left out of the land value.

That split is worth reading closely before a sale. If a well or septic system is failing or an outbuilding is gone, say so in a petition with photos or a repair estimate, because the petition asks for land and improvement values separately. The county also publishes 2025 sales data that you can filter by area to build a comparison.

Which relief programs can Lewis County owners use?

The senior and disabled persons exemption is the main program, and the Assessor's Office at 360-740-1392 administers it. Lewis County states that once the exemption is granted it does not need to be repaid. Under RCW 84.36.381, you qualify at 61 or older, when retired because of a disability, or as a veteran with the required VA rating, and you must own and live in the home. A surviving spouse or domestic partner can qualify from age 57 if the other spouse was receiving the exemption.

For owners in the lowest income tier, the statute fixes the valuation used for the exemption at the level in the year you first qualify, and it lets you transfer the exemption to a replacement home after a sale. Income limits and exempt amounts change for taxes payable in 2027, so ask the Assessor for the figures that apply to you. An owner turned down for the exemption can petition the Board of Equalization, using the form on the Board's forms page.

What should I expect at a Lewis County sale closing?

The Treasurer processes the real estate excise tax affidavit for deeded transfers. Lewis County asks for four printed copies of the affidavit, charges a $10 minimum to process one, and does not process transfers after 4 p.m., which gives the Auditor time to record before closing.

The state portion is graduated. For sales on or after January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue lists 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% from there to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above that. A local rate is added, and the county's REET page links the current local rates. The seller normally pays, and unpaid REET can become a lien on the property. Ask your escrow officer to request a tax payoff figure from the Treasurer before the closing date.

Call the Treasurer at 360-740-1115 for bills, payments and due dates, and the Assessor at 360-740-1392 for values and exemptions. The Board of Equalization takes appeals at 360-740-1391.

A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% interest per month and no penalty. Other property pays 1% per month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1.

Can I appeal my Lewis County property value online?

Yes. The Board of Equalization takes petitions through an online form, by mail, or in person at Room 210 of the Historic Courthouse. Attach a copy of your value change notice, and file one petition per parcel.

No. The county says the exemption does not need to be repaid once it is granted. A tax deferral is different, so ask the Assessor which program you hold before you sell.

Yes, but not after 4 p.m. Bring the excise tax affidavit copies early, and have your escrow officer confirm any tax payoff with the Treasurer ahead of time.

Where do Lincoln County, WA owners deal with property tax?

Everything runs through the courthouse at 450 Logan Street in Davenport. The Lincoln County Treasurer collects tax at PO Box 370, Davenport, WA 99122, and answers at 509-725-5061. The Assessor, at PO Box 400, values the property and can be reached at 509-725-7011 or 509-596-1454, Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

The Assessor's page states the legal standard: property is valued at 100% of true and fair market value, and each property must be physically inspected at least once every six years. The Assessor may reappraise sooner and may lower values when the market falls. Disagreements go to the County Board of Equalization.

The Treasurer takes mailed payments, online payments and payments by phone at 866-898-2915.

What should a seller know about Lincoln County's setting and market?

Lincoln County is a wide, thinly settled county on the Big Bend Plateau in eastern Washington, and its parcels are far apart. It sits on the Channeled Scablands at 1,500 to 2,500 feet above sea level. Summers are hot and dry, winters are cold, and rainfall ranges from about 8 inches in the west to about 20 inches in the northeast. Interstate 90, U.S. 2 and U.S. 395 cross the county.

Davenport is the county seat and the largest city. Harrington and Sprague are the other cities, and the towns are Almira, Creston, Odessa, Reardan and Wilbur. The county was created in November 1883 and is named for Abraham Lincoln. With about 2,310 square miles of land and 4.7 people per square mile, it is the fifth-least populous county in Washington.

Census QuickFacts give the housing picture:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 11,982, up 10.1% from April 2020.
  • Housing units: 6,178, with an owner-occupied rate of 80.4%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $292,800.
  • Median gross rent: $883. Median household income: $71,512.
  • Residents aged 65 and over: 28.5%.
  • Building permits in 2025: 67.

When are Lincoln County property taxes due?

Lincoln County bills are due April 30 and October 31, and in 2026 the second half was due Monday, November 2. The county's treasurer page posts that date, and it has now passed. If you still owe the second half on a parcel, interest is running.

The rules come from RCW 84.56.020. Tax of $50 or more can be paid in halves, and smaller bills are due in full on April 30. A mailed payment with no readable postmark that arrives within three business days of a due date is not delinquent. The treasurer may also accept partial payments and payment agreements, and any payment on delinquent years goes to the oldest year first unless you ask otherwise.

What does a late payment cost in Lincoln County?

The state sets the rates, and they follow the type of property. For a home with four or fewer units, interest is nine percent a year, charged monthly, with no penalty. For other real property and personal property, interest is twelve percent a year, plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an added 8% penalty on December 1 of the year the tax is due.

Two other provisions in the statute are worth knowing:

  • Delinquent owners must get a notice that names the statewide foreclosure hotline, and after two years the treasurer passes the owner's name and property address to a homeownership resource center.
  • An income-qualified owner who lives in the home can have interest and penalties waived shortly before the three-year point if the parcel is in a foreclosure action, once per property.

Call 509-725-5061 for a payoff statement for any parcel before you list it.

How does a Lincoln County assessment appeal work?

You file a petition with the Board of Equalization clerk by July 1 or within 30 days of the date the change of value notice was mailed, whichever is later. That 30-day period matches the statutory default in RCW 84.40.038. The county's Board page suggests asking the Assessor to re-inspect the property first, and the Assessor's Office will help with the petition form.

The Board's job is to find the market value on January 1 of the assessment year. You must show the Assessor erred and that the value does not match the market. Good evidence is sales of comparable property and maps or photographs that support your number. Other properties' assessments, the percentage of an increase, hardship and the tax amount cannot be considered.

The timeline is short. All evidence must be received at least 21 working days before the hearing, the hearing notice usually goes out 22 days in advance, and the decision usually arrives within two weeks. Bring copies, since anything presented becomes part of the record and is not returned. The Board must side with the Assessor unless your evidence is clear and convincing.

Which exemptions and programs can Lincoln County owners use?

The Assessor administers the senior citizen and disabled persons exemption and the current use program. For the exemption, the county explains that the value of your residence is frozen for tax purposes and you become exempt from excess and special levies and possibly regular levies. It covers a primary residence and up to one acre, and a mobile home can qualify even on rented land.

You must meet an age or disability test and own the home by December 31 of the year before the tax is due. For example, a 2026 exemption required ownership by December 31, 2025. You must have lived in the home at least six months by that date, and a copy of any trust that holds the home goes to the Assessor. The county notes that new medical deductions and a standard deduction have been added, and state law raises the thresholds for taxes payable in 2027, so ask for the current income limit instead of relying on an old brochure. The county links a screening tool from the state assessors' association.

RCW 84.36.381 lets a claimant move the exemption to a replacement residence after selling, which matters if you plan to buy again in the county.

What excise tax applies when a Lincoln County home sells?

The seller pays the Washington real estate excise tax, and it is due on the date of sale, not the recording date. The deed, the affidavit and the payment go to the county treasurer where the property sits, which in this county is the Treasurer in Davenport. The Department of Revenue warns that if the tax goes unpaid it can create a lien on the property.

If the tax is not paid within one month of the date of sale, interest runs from the sale date, and the 2026 and 2027 rate is 6%. The state portion for sales beginning January 1, 2027 is 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above. Farm and timber land that stays classified pays a flat 1.28% state rate. The Department of Revenue page also notes that the local rate is added. Ask the Treasurer for the local rate that applies to your parcel.

What is the Lincoln County tax title auction?

When a parcel is offered at foreclosure and draws no bid, it goes to the county as tax title property, and the county later resells it. Lincoln County scheduled its foreclosure and tax title auction for November 20, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. in the courthouse lobby, 450 Logan Street, with registration at 9:00 a.m.

The county's notice lists a parcel in the Town of Odessa with a minimum bid of $1,600, and shows a Town of Wilbur parcel withdrawn. If you own a parcel with years of unpaid tax, call the Treasurer before it reaches this stage.

File by July 1 or within 30 days of the mailing date on your change of value notice, whichever is later. Ask the Assessor to re-inspect first, because that can settle the question without a hearing.

Benton County by the numbers

Which Benton County offices deal with property tax?

The Benton County Treasurer collects the tax, and the Benton County Assessor sets the value. The Assessor's main office is in the Benton County Administration Building at 7122 W. Okanogan Pl., Building E, Kennewick, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A Prosser office keeps appointment-only hours on Tuesday to Thursday.

  • Assessor: 509-735-2394 in Kennewick or 509-786-2046 in Prosser. Washington law requires every parcel to be assessed at 100 percent of fair market value.
  • Treasurer: counters at the Prosser courthouse, 620 Market Street, second floor, and at the Kennewick administration building, suite E110. See the Treasurer's property tax page.
  • Board of Equalization: hears valuation appeals, and the Assessor's site links to it.

What is Benton County like for a home seller?

Benton County sits in south-central Washington with the Columbia River forming its north, south and east edges. It was created on March 8, 1905 from parts of Klickitat and Yakima counties and named for the Missouri statesman Thomas Hart Benton. Prosser is the county seat, but Kennewick is the most populous city. The other cities are Richland, West Richland and Benton City, and Finley is a census-designated place.

The Yakima River crosses the county from west to east and joins the Columbia at Richland. About one-third of the land is public, much of it the Hanford Site, and the Red Mountain wine district lies entirely inside the county. Higher education is local, with Washington State University Tri-Cities and a Columbia Basin College campus both in Richland, and six public school districts serve students.

The 2025 Census estimate is 221,722 residents, up from 206,873 in 2020. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home was worth $407,800, 67.6 percent of homes were owner-occupied and median household income was $89,874. The county recorded 1,663 building permits in 2025. Population density in 2020 was about 122 people per square mile.

How do you pay Benton County property tax, and what does it cost?

You can pay online, by mail, in person or through one of two automatic withdrawal plans. The Treasurer's page lists these costs, and the vendor fees apply whether you pay online or at the counter.

MethodCost or rule

Parcels that have reached the foreclosure stage cannot be paid online. After the Certificate of Delinquency is filed, the Treasurer takes payment in full by cash or cashier's check under RCW 84.64.070.

When are Benton County taxes due?

The whole year's tax is due on or before April 30, and you may pay half by April 30 and half by October 31. Bills under $50 are due in full on April 30. If either date lands on a weekend, the deadline moves to the following Monday, and mail is on time when it carries a postmark on or before the due date.

Interest and penalty are charged on the entire principal balance. Under RCW 84.56.020, a residential parcel with four or fewer units owes 9 percent a year with no penalties, while other parcels owe 12 percent plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1. The Treasurer's FAQ also says the law allows no extension for hardship, and that delinquency is not reported to credit agencies.

Benton billing has local quirks. Columbia Irrigation District and Kiona Irrigation District assessments share the property tax bill and must be paid together with it, so a mortgage servicer may adjust an escrow payment. Benton Irrigation District bills separately, with payment due April 1 and no interest or penalty until after April 30. The Kennewick Irrigation District collects its own money. Charges for weed control, soil conservation, mosquito control and horticultural pest and disease control also ride on the bill, and they create an enforceable lien.

Who pays what at a Benton County closing?

Taxes attach to the parcel, and the county states that its foreclosures are against the property. The Treasurer's FAQ puts the duty on the buyer to learn the tax status before purchase, and on both sides to decide how the year's tax is handled in the real estate closing.

Absent a contract term, RCW 84.60.020 divides the year by the sale date. The seller owes the fraction of the calendar year before the sale and the buyer owes the remainder. Since the county mails statements in the new year based on who owned the property on December 1, the FAQ suggests forwarding any statement you receive after closing to the new owner.

  • Order the tax status with the title or escrow company before the closing date.
  • Ask whether irrigation or special district charges are on the bill.
  • Real estate excise tax is due on the date of sale, regardless of when the deed is recorded. The seller normally pays it.
  • Legally changing the taxpayer name requires an excise tax affidavit filed with the Treasurer.

How do you appeal a Benton County valuation?

Contact the Assessor first, then file a petition with the Benton County Board of Equalization if the value still looks wrong. The state deadline in RCW 84.40.038 is July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the notice, or up to 60 days when the county has adopted that limit, whichever is later.

The Assessor's page explains why a higher value does not automatically raise a tax bill. It gives an example in which three homes rise 10, 20 and 15 percent while the district's levy grows only one percent. The rate falls from $1.00 to about $0.878 per $1,000, so the 10 percent home pays 3.39 percent less, the 20 percent home pays 5.39 percent more and the 15 percent home pays 1 percent more. What drives your bill is how your value changed compared with other properties in the district.

Anyone paying under protest to preserve a refund claim must follow RCW 84.68.020 and WAC 458-18-215. The Treasurer only keeps a file of the protest papers and does not judge whether they are legally sufficient.

Is there tax relief for Benton County seniors and disabled owners?

Yes. Owners who are at least 61, or retired because of a disability, and who own and live in the home may qualify for an exemption, and the Assessor takes the application. According to the Treasurer, people on the program are exempt from voted levies, which average about 40 percent of a Benton County tax bill. A deferral program for seniors lets the estate pay later.

The Assessor's forms page carries the exemption application, deferral applications for seniors and for limited-income homeowners, and an exemption for physical improvements to a single family home. Keep paying while an application is pending, since the Treasurer cannot change the amount due until the Assessor approves the change; a refund or revised bill follows.

When does Benton County foreclose for unpaid taxes?

Real property foreclosure starts once taxes are a full three years delinquent, and the process begins in June and ends with a sale in November. Any sale money beyond the taxes and costs goes to the former owner. Personal property is collected as soon as it turns delinquent, and the notice runs in a local newspaper's legal column.

More questions about Benton County, WA Property Tax Guide

When are property taxes due in Benton County, WA?

April 30 for the full year or the first half, and October 31 for the second half. A due date on a weekend moves to the following Monday. Bills under $50 are due in full on April 30.

Can I pay Benton County property tax by credit card?

Yes, with a 2.5 percent vendor fee on credit cards and non-Visa debit cards. E-check costs $1, and Visa debit costs $3.95 per transaction. The same fees apply when you pay at the counter.

How can I spread Benton County property tax over the year?

Use the monthly installment plan, which withdraws nine payments on the 15th for $0.75 each. Apply by January 5 for the first half or May 1 for the second half. The semi-annual ACH plan withdraws in April and October at no cost.

Who owes the tax when a Benton County house sells mid-year?

Unless the contract says otherwise, the seller owes the part of the year before the sale date and the buyer owes the rest under RCW 84.60.020. Settle the split in escrow and confirm the status with the Treasurer.

Can I appeal my Benton County property tax bill?

Yes, you can petition the Board of Equalization to change the assessed value. File a petition with the Board of Equalization by July 1, or within 30 days of the notice, or within the county's limit of up to 60 days, whichever is later.

Who bills and collects property tax in Stevens County?

The Stevens County Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the Stevens County Assessor sets the value it is based on. Both offices sit in the courthouse at 215 S Oak St in Colville, Washington.

  • Treasurer: Room 103, phone 509-684-2593, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Treasurer page lists treasurer@stevenscountywa.gov for email.
  • Assessor: Room 101, phone 509-684-6161, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Assessor handles valuation, exemptions and current use classification.
  • Board of Equalization clerk: Commissioner's building at 230 E. Birch St, phone 509-684-7513. Email the clerk for an appointment because office hours are limited.

If you own a house in Stevens County and are thinking about selling it, these three offices answer nearly every tax question you will have before closing.

What does Stevens County look like for a home seller?

Stevens County is a large, thinly settled county on the Canadian border in northeastern Washington. Colville is the county seat and the largest city, and most of the Spokane Indian Reservation lies inside the county line, according to Wikipedia. The county is part of the Spokane metropolitan area.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table shows 49,668 residents in July 2025 across 2,477 square miles of land, which works out to about 18.7 people per square mile in 2020. With so few people per square mile, the county is mostly rural land outside Colville.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 79.8 percent (2020 to 2024).
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $350,600.
  • Median household income: $69,327.
  • Residents 65 and over: 27.8 percent.

More than a quarter of residents are past 65, which makes the senior exemption and deferral programs described below relevant to many owners here.

When are Stevens County property taxes due?

Property tax is due April 30 and October 31, and the county treats the postmark as the payment date for mail. State law, RCW 84.56.020, allows you to pay half by April 30 and the rest by October 31 when your total is $50 or more. A bill under $50 is due in full on April 30.

The Treasurer's Property Tax page says the U.S. Post Office cancellation mark decides the date, so a postage meter date does not count. You can pay in person, by mail, in either of two drop boxes (one outside the Treasurer's office and a drive-up box behind the courthouse), or by card through the county's payment vendor, which charges its own fee. Returned checks carry a $25 service fee and void the payment for that parcel.

Sources: Stevens County Treasurer pages and RCW 84.56.020. Ask the Treasurer whether the Saturday, October 31, 2026 date moved to Monday, November 2, and what balance is still open on your parcel.

What happens if Stevens County property tax goes unpaid?

Late tax earns interest from the delinquency date, and a house can go to tax foreclosure once the oldest tax is three full years behind. Under RCW 84.56.020, the rate on residential property with four or fewer units is 9 percent a year, and penalties apply only to other kinds of property. Because the county's own page describes charges differently, ask the Treasurer for a written payoff figure before you rely on any estimate.

Stevens County's Tax Foreclosure Sale page describes the 2026 process in detail:

  • The 2026 sale was set for December 4, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., held online, covering parcels with the 2023 tax year unpaid.
  • An owner can redeem at any time up to the close of business the day before the sale.
  • Real property tax holds first lien position, so a foreclosure can wipe out a deed of trust, mortgage or judgment. Local improvement district assessments and IRS liens stay with the property.
  • Properties that do not sell go to the county as tax title property.

The Treasurer's page adds that a title search on each foreclosure parcel costs about $350 and is added to the redemption amount. Statute also requires the treasurer to waive interest and penalties for an income-qualified owner-occupant whose home is in foreclosure, once, if the Assessor verifies eligibility.

If you are past due and want to sell before the sale date, call 509-684-2593 for the redemption total and give that figure to your escrow officer.

How do you appeal a Stevens County assessment?

You file a petition with the Stevens County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within the window after your value notice was mailed, whichever is later. The county's Board of Equalization page gives that window as 30 days from the mailing date on the Assessor's change of value notice, and state law in RCW 84.40.038 lets a county adopt a limit of up to 60 days. Read the deadline printed on your own notice and call the clerk if the dates look different.

The board is three private citizens, plus up to four alternates, appointed by the county commissioners. It also hears denials of senior and disabled exemptions, current use decisions and forest land classifications.

  • Send a copy of everything you file to the Assessor as well.
  • A faxed or emailed petition only protects the deadline. The signed original must follow.
  • Missing the deadline may still leave a late-filing request under WAC 458-14-056, so contact the clerk.

Pay your tax on time while an appeal is open. Any change to the value shows up on a later bill or as a refund.

What tax relief can Stevens County homeowners use?

Washington's senior and disability exemption is run by the county Assessor, and the Department of Revenue's exemption page sets the basic tests. You must own and live in the home as your primary residence, have qualifying income, and by December 31 of the assessment year be one of the following:

  • At least 61 years old.
  • At least 57 and the surviving spouse or domestic partner of someone who was in the program.
  • Unable to work because of a disability, at any age.
  • A veteran with a service-connected rating of at least 40 percent, or compensated at the 100 percent rate.

Income limits are set county by county, so call the Stevens County Assessor at 509-684-6161 for the current figure and the application. The Assessor's office treats income and expense details from these applications as confidential records, according to its FAQ page.

Washington also has a deferral program in which the state pays the tax for you and takes a lien. The state program description says the deferred tax plus interest must be repaid when you no longer own and live in the home, so a sale brings that lien into closing. Ask the Assessor for the payoff early.

How is property tax handled when you sell a Stevens County house?

Washington divides the current year's tax between buyer and seller by days owned unless the contract says otherwise. RCW 84.60.020 says the lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, and that when a contract is silent the seller pays the share of the calendar year before the sale date and the buyer pays the rest.

In practice the escrow officer asks the Treasurer for the status of both halves, collects your share from proceeds, and pays whatever is open. Before you list or accept an offer, do three things:

  • Look up the parcel on the Stevens County property search to see what is paid.
  • Ask the Treasurer whether any prior year is delinquent, because a clean current year does not clear an older balance.
  • Ask the Assessor whether an exemption, deferral or current use classification is on the parcel and what ending it would cost.

More questions about Stevens County, WA Property Tax Guide

When is the second half of Stevens County property tax due?

October 31, with the postmark deciding mailed payments. In 2026 that date was a Saturday, so the due date moved to Monday, November 2, which has passed. The Treasurer at 509-684-2593 can tell you what is still open.

Can I pay Stevens County property tax in two halves?

Yes, when the total is $50 or more. Pay half by April 30 and the remainder by October 31. Totals under $50 must be paid in full by April 30, per RCW 84.56.020.

How long can Stevens County property tax go unpaid before foreclosure?

Three full years. The county's 2026 sale covered parcels with the 2023 tax year unpaid and was set for December 4, 2026. An owner can redeem until the business day before the sale.

How do I appeal my Stevens County property value?

File a petition with the Board of Equalization by July 1 or by the date tied to your notice mailing. The county's page states 30 days from the notice date. Contact the clerk at 509-684-7513 and send a copy to the Assessor.

Does a sale clear the property tax lien in Stevens County?

The tax is paid from your closing proceeds. The lien attaches each January 1, so the escrow officer will confirm the current year share and any delinquent year with the Treasurer before the deed records.
